key_insight: Nonlinear X-ray parametric down-conversion selectively probes radiation-induced dynamics in MAPbBr3, revealing behavior distinct from conventional Bragg diffraction.
engineering_relevance: Comparing nonlinear and linear X-ray responses could help distinguish radiation-driven changes in hybrid perovskites that conventional diffraction alone may not resolve.
method: Measure X-ray-to-ultraviolet parametric down-conversion during continuous irradiation of a MAPbBr3 single crystal.
Compare minute-timescale PDC and Bragg diffraction dynamics.
Use density functional theory to assess electronic contributions and bromide-vacancy effects.
evidence_signal: Both signals show slow decay consistent with diffusion-driven damage, but reach different steady states; only Bragg diffraction shows an additional fast decay, while calculations implicate methylammonium N 2s states in PDC.
watch_item: The intrinsically weak PDC signal requires high photon flux, making measurement-induced damage an important constraint.
paper_title: X-ray parametric down-conversion probes radiation-induced dynamics in hybrid perovskite MAPbBr3
